sections.Item 1: Item 1. Business. NVIDIA pioneered accelerated computing to help solve the most challenging computational problems. Our full-stack includes GPUs, networking, systems, and the CUDA programming model and software libraries, on which millions of developers have built applications; this installed base and ecosystem is a significant competitive advantage. Data Center revenue represented approximately 87% of total revenue in fiscal 2026, up from 78% in fiscal 2025, driven by demand for our platforms for generative AI training and inference from cloud service providers, consumer internet companies and enterprises. We sell through cloud service providers, OEMs, ODMs, system integrators and distributors. Demand for our data center products continued to exceed supply for the majority of the fiscal year, and we have entered into long-term supply and capacity agreements with our foundry and memory partners. sections.Item 1A: Item 1A. Risk Factors. Our revenue is concentrated: sales to a small number of large customers represent a significant portion of revenue — in fiscal 2026 three direct customers each represented more than 10% of revenue and together approximately 40% of total revenue, and the loss of or reduction in purchases by any of them could materially and adversely affect our results. This concentration increased compared with the prior year. Several of our largest customers are developing their own internal AI accelerators and may reduce purchases of our products if those efforts succeed. We depend on third-party foundries and memory suppliers, principally located in Taiwan and Korea, and supply constraints or geopolitical events could disrupt our ability to meet demand. Export controls on advanced computing products to certain countries have reduced and may further reduce our addressable market. Our growth rates have been exceptionally high and are unlikely to be sustained; if demand for AI infrastructure moderates, our revenue growth could decelerate significantly and our stock price could decline. sections.Item 7: Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis. Revenue for fiscal 2026 was $211.0 billion, up 62% from $130.5 billion in fiscal 2025, which itself had grown 114% from fiscal 2024. Data Center revenue growth was driven by demand for our accelerated computing platforms for large language model training and inference. Gross margin was 74.2%, down slightly from the prior year due to product mix and higher costs of new platforms. Operating income was $122.6 billion. Free cash flow was $58.9 billion. We ended the year with $38.0 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and $9.7 billion of notes outstanding, all fixed-rate, with no maturities before fiscal 2028; we returned capital through share repurchases and dividends. Our backlog and customer commitments for our next-generation platform were higher than at the same point last year. We expect continued strong demand but note that quarterly growth rates will moderate as the base grows. Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis.
